design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (Ironwood Machining Inc., Meadowlark Business Standard, MN_CSG / Xcel Energy)

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one thing: pay, today, the security deposit his pending 15 kW increase needs. The deposit cannot be priced from his request: its rule says it is not fixed until the ledger carries a charge, actual or estimated, for every statement month whose estimate waiting period has passed. Statement month 2026-08 ended 52 days ago with neither a credit nor a charge, so the agent must find that gap in the credits and billing ledger, work out that only the late-statement estimate write closes it, price that estimate (six factors over the subscription's own charges, outstanding estimates, reversals, history, share and credit rates) and only then price the deposit (six factors including the garden share's payment record in another line). Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling ledgers and calculating.

2. SCOPE. Occupied by task 0: biz_ext_guarantee_trueup, biz_ext_decrease_amendment_fee and their tools. Claimed here: biz_ext_late_statement_estimate (agent, bill_statement_estimate_b08e308f) and biz_ext_increase_deposit (user, pay_increase_deposit_a318506d). Together the two tasks cover all four extended policies; scopes are disjoint.

3. PROBLEM TREE (draw: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,6]).
- Root: biz_ext_increase_deposit (on_request; owner=user per owner_ruling (b): holder-completed payment through the secure payment flow; the rule says the payment method is never on file and staff never take account numbers; the persona pays by ACH himself).
- Prerequisite: biz_ext_late_statement_estimate (state_due; agent).
- Edge: kind value_input, gate monthly_estimate, form state. Prerequisite sentence (negated direction, the way a deposit desk says it waits on a complete ledger): "The increase deposit is not fixed until the billing ledger carries a subscription charge, actual or estimated, for every statement month whose estimate waiting period has passed." Four-point test: connective "not ... until"; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (a charge row per statement month past its waiting period, defined by the rule's sentence "A statement month's estimate waiting period passes estimate_wait_days calendar days after the month ends."); no tool, id or code token; scope "every statement month" equals the condition. Within this difficulty only the estimate write books a charge for a month with no posted credit, so the state names one action. Derivation: sentence + find_biz_credits (no 2026-07 or 2026-08 posting) + find_biz_billing (an estimate stands for 2026-07, nothing for 2026-08) + the estimate rule -> bill the 2026-08 estimate first.
- False at the opening: initial_state.biz_billing.<2026-07 estimate>.billing_month = 2026-07 is the latest estimate; initial_state.biz_credits.<2026-09 posting>.statement_month = 2026-09 is the latest posting; no row of either table carries 2026-08.
- Deletion sensitivity (run): without the estimate the deposit's three-month window holds two charges (426.71 and 359.33) -> deposit 670.30 instead of 579.75, and the ledger lacks the 2026-08 estimate.
- Order: estimate (step 14) then payment (step 16); single chain. user_scenario never mentions statements, estimates, late fees or the garden ledger; tools check nothing.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. biz_evt_subscription_charge.billable_status: status active. one_charge_per_credit binds a charge to a posted credit line; an estimate has none, so its evidence contract can never bind (BLUEPRINT-KNOWN); routed with a declared self-scoped overwrite that keeps the sentence for every posted line and states one estimate per statement month. The base estimate sentence (average of the last three actual charges) is overwritten for estimates with this policy's basis and levels, keeping the waiting period, the no-credit-reference rule and the two-in-a-row limit (the run ended with the 2026-09 actual charge, so a 2026-08 estimate is allowed). biz_evt_security_deposit.deposit_required_only: credit_review deposit_required. The base deposit formula (contract_kw x yield x estimated rate) is overwritten for increase deposits only; release rules stay in force (late fees fell in every 12-month run, so the 703.80 deposit is still held). biz_allocation_change: the increase (15 kW, received 2026-10-19, 20 months after activation, first change of contract year 2, 45 kW <= 50 kW max) is filed in 2026-11 after the deposit; no gold action files it.

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Holding: the one biz subscription (30.00 kW). Estimate object: statement month 2026-08 of that subscription. Basis rows: actual charges invoiced after 2026-07-22 (one: 2026-09, 359.33) and, widened, after 2026-04-22 (five: 2026-04, 2026-05, the 2026-03 re-posting, 2026-06, 2026-09); excluded: the original 2026-03 charge (invoiced 2026-04-18, before the widened window, and offset by its reversal correction), the 2026-07 estimate (not an actual charge). Deposit object: the 15 kW increase request; window charges after 2026-07-22 including estimates. Cross-line object: the Garden Business Fixed 15 share (12 kW) and its late fee of 2026-03-30.

6. FACTOR CARD — estimate (result 315.33; all-baseline 359.33). thin_basis_widening (method, R6): one actual charge in the window -> widened six-month average 409.136 (baseline 359.33) -> 276.95 under baseline. outstanding_estimate_level (parameter, R6): one outstanding estimate -> 85% -> 370.98. reversal_history_level (parameter, R6): one reversal in 12 months -> 95% -> 331.93. history_length_level (parameter, R2/R6): 20 months since activation -> 95% -> 331.93. share_size_estimate_level (parameter, R1 share band): 30 kW -> 98.5% -> 320.14. credit_rate_step_level (parameter, R6): 2026 rate 1.9% above the year-earlier postings -> 102% -> 309.15. Near-miss: the 2026-06 charge invoiced 2026-07-18 sits just outside the basis window.
FACTOR CARD — deposit (result 579.75; all-baseline 367.12). payment_record_months (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty garden, base-grounded on the release rule's late-fee test): dual billing AND (1 own late fee within 12 months OR the garden late fee of 2026-03-30) -> 3 months -> 422.81 under baseline; near-miss: the 2025-08-27 late fee is 13 months old. returned_payment_months (parameter, R6): one returned ACH payment -> +0.5 -> 501.28. enlarged_share_band (parameter, R1): 45 kW -> x0.95 -> 608.67. increase_depth_level (parameter, R6): 50% of the share -> x1.2 -> 488.20. remaining_term_level (parameter, R2): 15 months left -> x0.75 -> 762.86. held_deposit_adjustment (method): held 703.80 below the current requirement 734.25 -> +30.45 -> 549.31.
No factor reads another factor's binding: shared selections (window charges, monthly estimate, share on file, added kW) are plain bindings.

7. WORLD ROWS. customers/utility_accounts/projects: identity; account active, authorized, usage 96400 kWh; both projects (biz MN_CSG with 42.50 kW unallocated; garden project). biz_subscriptions: Standard plan, dual, deposit_required, deposit 703.80, activation 2025-02-12, term end 2028-02-11. biz_allocations: single 30 kW filing. biz_credits: postings from activation; 2026-07 and 2026-08 never reported (metering dispute at the project); the 2026-03 posting reversed 2026-05-08 and re-posted 2026-05-22. biz_billing: one charge per posting (credit x 90%), the reversal-correction credit, payments, two late fees (2025-08-27, 2026-06-29), the returned 2026-01 ACH payment with its 30.00 fee and re-payment inside grace, the 2026-07 estimate 426.71 (priced under the estimate rule as of 2026-09-15) paid, and the 2024-11-18 deposit line. biz_reviews: contract year 1 (no guarantee, no resize). biz_requests: the 15 kW increase. garden_subscriptions/credits/billing: the 12 kW garden share activated 2025-11-13 (no garden anniversary yet), its postings, charges at the fixed contract rate, payments and one late fee.

8. PERSONA. Teodoro Castellanos, calm and formal; volunteers the goal (pay the deposit for the 15 kW increase he requested online) and nothing else; identity on request (phone 6515550131, ZIP 55418, email alternative); garden share only if asked; pays by ACH through the portal himself with the amount the agent states; never gives account numbers; ends after the deposit is confirmed.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION. Verify; read subscription, request, credits, billing, filings, true-up, garden share/billing/credits, utility account, projects; bill the 2026-08 estimate (315.33, due 2026-11-21); compute the deposit with that estimate in the window (monthly estimate 367.1233, 3.5 months, x0.95 x1.2 x0.75, plus the 30.45 shortfall) = 579.75; hand over the payment step (ach, 579.75).

10. VERIFICATION. evalc.py (gate DSL) reproduces 315.33 and 579.75, the per-factor figures above, 670.30 with the estimate skipped, and the seeded 2026-07 estimate 426.71 as of 2026-09-15. Gates for task 1: EXTENDED / TASK TOOL CONTRACT / REPLAY / SOLVABILITY / COMPUTE / GROUNDING / SCOPE OK.

11. EASY MISTAKES. Pricing the deposit before the estimate (670.30); averaging only the single in-window charge; counting the 2026-07 estimate as an actual charge in the estimate basis; using the original 2026-03 charge; using the plan's 2 deposit months without the garden late fee; counting the 13-month-old late fee; forgetting the held-deposit shortfall.

12. CLOSURE. biz_ext_late_statement_estimate -> bill_statement_estimate_b08e308f -> step 14 estimated_charge 315.33 -> estimated charge row for 2026-08; biz_ext_increase_deposit -> pay_increase_deposit_a318506d -> step 16 deposit_amount 579.75 -> deposit-held line and deposit_held_usd 1283.55. required_documents equal charter_scope.extended_policies.
user_scenario:
You are Teodoro Castellanos, owner of Ironwood Machining Inc. in northeast Minneapolis. You are calm, methodical and a little formal, the kind of person who reads every line of a statement, and you are calling Meadowlark Community Solar from the shop office late on a Thursday afternoon. The shop just put in a second CNC line, so on Monday you went on Meadowlark's website and asked to add 15 kilowatts to the shop's business solar share. Meadowlark then emailed that a security deposit has to be held before the increase can be filed, and that you would need to pay it yourself. You want to pay that deposit today so the increase can go ahead. You open with something like: "Good afternoon, this is Teodoro Castellanos with Ironwood Machining. On Monday I asked online to add 15 kilowatts to our solar share, and your email says there's a security deposit to pay before you can file it. I'd like to pay that deposit today."

You share details only when the agent asks for them. The phone number on the account is 6515550131 and the billing ZIP code is 55418; if the agent asks for an email instead, it is teo@ironwoodmachining.com. You have no account or reference numbers to hand and tell the agent to find you by the phone number. If asked which share, it is the shop's business solar share on the Xcel account at 2276 Central Avenue NE. Only if the agent asks whether the business holds anything else with Meadowlark do you mention the small fixed-rate garden share on the same Xcel account. If the agent confirms that 15 kilowatts is the increase you asked for, you say yes.

You do not know how the deposit is worked out and you never guess at an amount. If the agent tells you something has to be booked on the account before the deposit can be set, you say that is fine and to go ahead. You pay the deposit yourself, by ACH from the shop's bank account through the secure payment portal: once the agent hands you the payment step and tells you the amount, you run it with that amount and ACH as the method. You will not read out any bank or card numbers and you say so if asked. Once the payment has gone through and the agent confirms the deposit is held, you thank them and end the call without bringing up anything else.

edges.condition: biz_billing carries a biz_charge_billed row (actual, through its credit line, or estimated, through its billing_month) for every statement month of the subscription that ended more than estimate_wait_days calendar days before the frozen date.
edges.policy_source: The increase deposit is not fixed until the billing ledger carries a subscription charge, actual or estimated, for every statement month whose estimate waiting period has passed.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Statement month 2026-08 ended on 2026-08-31; its 45-day waiting period passed on 2026-10-15, yet the ledger has neither a credit posting nor a charge for it: the latest estimate covers 2026-07 and the latest posting is the 2026-09 statement.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The write of step 14 creates the estimated charge for billing_month 2026-08 (315.33) dated 2026-10-22; it is the third charge invoiced in the three whole months the deposit's monthly estimate averages.
